target.title: fix(outbound): restore current-conversation binding map when persist fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plugin channels that use the generic current-conversation
binding (any channel without a custom binding adapter) could route inbound
messages to the wrong or a deleted session target after a failed durable write.

The binding mutators — bind, touch, unbind, and expiry prune-on-read — update the
process-wide in-memory binding map first and then persist it to SQLite. If the
persist throws (disk full, read-only DB, transaction failure), the map is left
ahead of disk. Because the map is only loaded from disk once per process
(`bindingsLoaded` is a one-time flag), the diverged bindings are then served for
the rest of the process lifetime — until a restart — even though the caller
already received the error. Inbound messages get delivered to a stale binding
(a resolved session that was actually unbound, or a target that never persisted).

The one-time load path has the same weakness in the other direction: it flips
`bindingsLoaded` and clears the map before the DB read completes, so a failing
initial read latches an empty cache until restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each mutating path now snapshots the in-memory map, and if the durable write
throws it restores that snapshot before rethrowing, so runtime state never drifts
ahead of disk. This mirrors the rollback pattern already merged for the cron
scheduler in #99960 (`persistOrRestore` in `src/cron/service/ops.ts`). The
unbind-by-session path snapshots after its expiry scan settles (that scan can
itself persist prune deletes), so a later batch failure cannot resurrect a
binding the scan already dropped from disk. The one-time load now reads into a
local first and marks the cache loaded only after the read succeeds.

Scope is deliberately narrow: no change to the write mechanism, the store schema,
or the broader session-binding surface. The snapshot is a shallow map copy, which
is sufficient because records are always replaced wholesale (never mutated in
place), keeping the hot binding paths cheap.

## User Impact

Operators no longer end up with a process serving conversation bindings that
disagree with what is on disk after a transient storage failure. A failed
mutation now leaves the in-memory state exactly as it was before
the attempt, and the error still surfaces to the caller. No config, API, or
behavior change on the success path.

Affected paths: bind, touch, unbind by binding id, unbind by target session
key, and the expiry prune-on-read.

## Evidence

Focused fault-injection tests (`src/infra/outbound/current-conversation-bindings.test.ts`)
mock the durable write to throw and assert the in-memory map is restored for each
mutating path (bind, touch, unbind-by-id, unbind-by-session, prune-on-read), plus
the mixed unbind-by-session case where an expired binding is pruned mid-scan
before the batch fails, and a failing initial load that must not latch an empty
cache. This is the same proof shape used and merged for the cron rollback in
#99960 (`src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`, "cron service ops persist rollback").

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/current-conversation-bindings.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)   # 10 existing + 7 new
```
